ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey) base comprising approximately 80% of surface area, with high-intensity (white) features concentrated at distal tips and discrete interior coordinates.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity contiguous mottling clusters at left and right distal tips; approximately 10 discrete circular white ring-shaped blobs (rosettes) distributed across the central and right mid-sections; diffuse light-grey mottle-blobs on the left-central lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Obtuse V-shaped depression with an internal pixel angle of approximately 142 degrees and a shallow depth-to-width ratio relative to the lobe span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, stochastic serration pattern along the entire trailing edge; pixel-amplitudes range from 3 to 18 pixels forming sharp peaks and jagged valleys, particularly dense on the inner margins of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Sigmoidal curve with initial convexity near the median notch transitioning to a slight concavity before reaching the upturned distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Detection of multiple high-contrast circular white rings (barnacle scars) distributed asymmetrically: 4 in the right mid-lobe, 3 in the central region, and 2 in the upper-left quadrant.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several unaligned light-intensity linear disruptions; one notable diagonal scratch on the mid-left lobe and three shorter, vertical rake-like marks on the lower-right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive clusters of raised, high-intensity barnacle colonies (Coronula diadema) localized on the outer margins of both distal tips; multiple circular parasitic attachment scars across the ventral plane.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique 'beaded' peripheral contour at the fluke tips caused by dense barnacle clustering, creating significant deviation from the smooth natural lobe boundary.
